definitions.ask: Should Ctrl+Shift+B get its own new command instead of rebinding `edit-task-dependencies`?

choices.label: New `task-card-depends-on` command; `edit-task-dependencies` stays an unbound direct stage
Rebind `edit-task-dependencies` to the Task Card `b` route; its palette behavior changes

definitions.why: Additive; leaves the documented, tested palette direct-entry contract alone

definitions.ask: If `b` is unavailable (e.g. a non-#task bullet), keep the Task Card open after the notice, as `b` does?

choices.label: Show the notice and leave the Task Card open, exactly as pressing `b` does
Show the same notice and close the card, so a refused chord leaves no modal open

definitions.why: Bryan asked for Ctrl+Shift+B to behave just like Ctrl+Shift+P then `b`
